record.original_question: Given a non-trivial virtual knot K, can one prove that there exists a minimal realization of K in a thickened surface N = S_g x I together with an unknotted embedding of N into R^3 such that the resulting classical knot in R^3 is non-trivial?

evidence.quote: Given a non-trivial virtual knot K. Prove that there exists a minimal realization of K in N = Sg × I and an unknotted embedding of N ⊂ R3 such that the obtained classical knot in R3 is not trivial.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a non-trivial virtual knot. By a theorem of Kuperberg, $K$ admits a representative as a knot in a thickened orientable closed surface $N = \Sigma_g \times I$ (where $I = [0,1]$) of minimal genus $g$, and this minimal-genus thickened-surface representative is unique up to homeomorphism of the thickened surface and isotopy of the knot. Such a representative is called a minimal realization of $K$.

An embedding $\iota \colon N \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ of the thickened surface into 3-space is called unknotted if it extends to an embedding of a standardly embedded (unknotted) handlebody of genus $g$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given any embedding $\iota \colon N \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ and a knot $k \subset N$, one obtains a classical knot $\iota(k) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$.

Prove or disprove: for every non-trivial virtual knot $K$, there exist a minimal realization $k \subset N = \Sigma_g \times I$ of $K$ and an unknotted embedding $\iota \colon N \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ such that the resulting classical knot $\iota(k) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is non-trivial.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on virtual knots, minimal-genus surface representations (Kuperberg's theorem), and unknotted embeddings of thickened surfaces in R^3 do not reveal a published resolution of this specific question. The related theory (Kuperberg uniqueness, virtualization, bracket polynomial detection of non-classicality) is well developed, but no source verifies the asserted existence statement in full generality, nor a counterexample. Status appears unresolved as far as available evidence shows.

status_evidence.title: Minimal surface representations of virtual knots and links
status_evidence.snippet: A virtual knot diagram corresponds to a unique embedding in a thickened surface of minimal genus (Kuperberg's theorem on topological uniqueness of minimal representatives).
status_evidence.claim: The minimal-genus thickened-surface realization of a virtual knot is well-defined and unique.

status_evidence.title: Virtual knot - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Virtual knots are equivalence classes of knots in thickened surfaces under stabilization; Kuperberg showed the minimal genus representative is unique.
status_evidence.claim: Background on minimal realizations confirms the setup; no resolution of the stated existence problem is recorded.
